block_node.block_desc:
Orbit location of interest using a UAV.
The Pose input is a 4x1 matrix containing the current [x,y,z] position and course angle of the UAV. The Center and Radius inputs define the circular orbit location as an [x,y,z] vector and radius as a scalar value. The TurnDirection input specifies the direction around the circle, where a positive value indicates a clockwise turn as viewed from above. A negative value indicates a counter-clockwise turn and 0 automatically determines the direction. The LookaheadDistance input is a positive scalar to control how closely the UAV follows the circular path. Small values improve tracking, but can lead to oscillations in the path.
Set the UAV type parameter for your specific UAV type. The External reset parameter allows you to use a rising signal to trigger a reset of the NumTurns output port. The optional output ports can be enabled using the checkboxes in Output parameters. NumTurns indicates how many times the UAV has completed the orbit. By default, changing the orbit center or radius triggers a reset.

Calculate the lookahead point, desired course, desired yaw and lookahead flag from the current UAV position using the pose, the set of waypoints and the lookahead distance.
The Waypoints input accepts a set of waypoints as either an Nx3, Nx4, or Nx5 matrix, where N is the number of waypoints. Each row is an [x y z] position vector with optional yaw angle and transition radius for the UAV. The LookaheadDistance input is a positive scalar that controls how closely the UAV follows the path. A smaller lookahead distance improves path tracking, but can lead to oscillations in the path.
To specify the same transition radius for each waypoint, choose "internal" for the Transition radius source and specify the Transition radius in the block mask. Choose "external" to specify a different transition radius in each row of the Waypoints input. To specify a yaw angle for each waypoint, select Show yaw input variable.
The CrossTrackError optional port outputs the cross-track error and the Status optional port output indicates if the UAV has reached the final waypoint.

Compute an obstacle-free direction using range sensor data and a target position.
The Position input is a 3x1 vector [x y z] of the UAV position. The Orientation input is a 4x1 vector [w x y z] of the orientation of the UAV expressed as a quaternion. The ObstaclePoints input is a Nx3 matrix representing the position of the obstacles, where N is the number of obstacle points. The TargetPosition input is the 3x1 vector [x y z] of the position of the target.
Set the sensor and vehicle parameters in the Main tab. Use the Histogram tab to specify the histogram parameters and the Cost tab to specify the cost parameters.

Generate minimum jerk polynomial trajectories through multiple waypoints.
The Time input is a scalar or a vector, the Waypoints input is an NxP matrix and the TimePoints input is a P-element vector.
The block generates minimum jerk polynomial trajectories that pass through the waypoints at the times specified in TimePoints. Select the Show boundary conditions input ports to specify the boundary conditions as NxP matrices. Select the Show polynomial coefficients output port and Show status output port checkboxes to enable the optional outputs. Select the Time allocation checkbox to enable time allocation and its associated parameters.
The initial and final values of q, qd, qdd, and qddd are held constant outside of the time period defined by TimePoints.

The Time input is a scalar or a vector, the Waypoints input is an NxP matrix and the TimePoints input is a P-element vector.

Select the Show boundary conditions input ports to specify the boundary conditions as NxP matrices.
